messages:
Taylor: kicking off dedicated canary for halberd18b-int4 — seeing intermittent OOMs on warm traffic (avg input ~350 tokens).
Ash: frequency? single canary pool?
Taylor: canary pool only; 2 OOMs in first 10m. log: ```[2026-03-22T15:12:04Z] ERROR oom: alloc failed at kv_cache_grow model=halberd18b-int4 pool=gpu0 config: batch_size=4, window=12, max_new_tokens=1024, prefetch=true, slot_reserve=0.05 trace: alloc 3.2GB -> failed```
infra-bot: canary-run=cr-20260322-halb-can1 runtime=0.14.0 events=2
Mira: int4 + max_new_tokens=1024 is risky for fragmentation on 18b family.
Kevin: operationally we usually set max_new_tokens=512 and cap batch_size=2 during warmup; bump slot_reserve to ~0.12 for int4.
Taylor: micro-bench vs int8 (50 prompts): int8 p50=210ms tps=280, int4 p50=230ms tps=300. quick eval (100 prompts) shows ~-1.8% rouge-L for int4.
Ash: small throughput win for int4 but quality dip + frag risk. Not a clear win.
Mira: mitigations: upgrade runtime (0.14.2 has slab compaction + soft-evict), lower max_new_tokens default, raise slot_reserve, try session_cache=false, or fallback to int8 for critical routes.
Kevin: plan: upgrade canary runtime to 0.14.2, run 2h soak with config: max_new_tokens=512, batch_size=2, slot_reserve=0.12, session_cache=false, kv_trim_threshold=0.6, adaptive_window=on. add alerts for OOM spike >1/min and p95>1s.
Taylor: repro curl used earlier included max_new_tokens=1024; will re-run with 512 and session_cache=false.
Ash: also test with prefetch disabled to isolate prefetch-driven KV churn.
Kevin: if soak still OOMs, I'll start quant packer bisect (per-layer activations can outlier).
Mira: after soak run paired 500-prompt eval: int8 baseline vs int4 candidate. if int4 rouge-L drop >1% consider mixed fallback or revert.
infra-bot: soak queued soak-6312345670-1 owner=Taylor team=eng-ml
Taylor: starting soak in ~10m, will report soak metrics+eval numbers here. :rocket:
